item.title: Trump says Iran agrees to hand over ‘nuclear dust’
item.summary: Iran has not confirmed Trump’s claim. Giving up its highly enriched uranium would be a major step toward an agreement.

item.title: Even for Europe’s populist firebrands, Trump is going too far
item.summary: The symbiosis between the president and European nationalists has reached a potential breaking point as he issues genocidal rhetoric and criticizes the pope.

item.title: Airstrike by Nigeria, a U.S. ally against Islamist militants, kills scores
item.summary: Villagers, health workers and human rights monitors see a pattern of reckless attacks in the U.S.-backed fight against Boko Haram and its Islamic State-affiliated offshoot.

item.title: Iran disputes claims of new agreements with Trump
item.summary: Tehran put limits on the Strait of Hormuz’s opening, as the United States issued a new sanctions exemption on the sale of Russian oil.

item.title: Displaced Lebanese families rush home as fragile ceasefire takes force
item.summary: Even amid uncertainty over whether the truce would hold, many in Lebanon expressed relief at the prospect of quiet as aid groups mobilized help.

item.title: 10-day ceasefire in Lebanon begins as Israel agrees to U.S.-backed deal
item.summary: President Donald Trump announced the agreement, which went into force Thursday evening, as Pakistani mediators worked to extend a U.S.-Iran ceasefire and arrange new talks.

item.title: Pope Leo decries ‘tyrants’ ravaging world, days after insults from Trump
item.summary: The pontiff did not name the president during a speech in Cameroon. He criticized those who manipulate religion “for their own military, economic or political gain.”

item.title: One of the world’s most wanted men is arrested, ending years-long hunt
item.summary: Daniel Joseph Kinahan, a fugitive suspected of leading a powerful gang in Ireland, was arrested in Dubai as part of a secret operation by Irish and UAE police.

item.title: South African politician who drew Trump’s ire sentenced on gun charges
item.summary: Julius Malema, whose incendiary rhetoric about Afrikaners drew notice on the U.S. right, was handed a five-year prison term for firing a gun at a 2018 rally.

item.title: House votes to restore protections for Haitians, defying Trump
item.summary: Ten House Republicans joined Democrats to oppose President Donald Trump on his immigration policy Thursday, voting to restore temporary protections for Haitians living in the United States.
